sentences.text: ORAL ORDER
Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

The present petition is preferred by the in-laws of the complainant seeking quashment of the F.I.R.
registered under Sections 498A, 294(B), and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, read with Sections 4 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
It is pertinent to note that though the husband of the complainant has also been named as an accused in the impugned F.I.R., he has not joined as a petitioner in the present proceedings.

From the submissions advanced by the learned advocates appearing for the parties, it emerges that the husband and wife are now residing together, and the matrimonial discord between them appears to have been resolved.
They are now living separately from the petitioner in-laws.

Learned advocate Mr. Deepak N. Khanchandani has invited NEUTRAL CITATION Harshaben Chandarkumar Badlani vs State Of Gujarat on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71947911/
1 R/CR.MA/21772/2021 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined attention to Annexure-B -- an agreement whereby the petitioners (in-laws) are stated to have agreed to pay an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month to the complainant and her husband towards rent.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION Harshaben Chandarkumar Badlani vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no such amount is paid by the in-laws.
Prima facie, the nature of allegations and the contents of the agreement do not disclose the essential ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 498A of the IPC against the petitioners.

Moreover, the alleged grievance arising out of a private rent-related agreement between adult parties -- which includes the complainant and her husband jointly seeking monetary contribution from the in- laws -- cannot, by any stretch of legal interpretation, attract the rigours of penal provisions under Section 498A.
The dispute appears to be civil in nature and does not disclose commission of any cognizable offence against the present petitioners.

On overall consideration of the facts, and upon perusal of the F.I.R., this Court is of the prima facie opinion that continuation of the criminal proceedings against the present petitioners would amount to abuse of process of law, warranting interference under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Accordingly, the present petition is allowed.
The F.I.R., being I-C.R. No.50 of 2019 registered with Mahila Police Station (East), Ahmedabad, along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, is hereby quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.
